newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S.-Venezuelan consortium wins Colombian plant.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Venezuelan consortium wins Colombian plant.

text.p: Friday's winning $535 million bid for the government's 56.7 percent stake in one of Colombia's top power companies was the result of a strategic partnership between two major players in the United States and Venezuelan energy markets, company officials said.
Juan Fernando Bonilla, head of Colombia's power plant privatization program, originally said the bid was made exclusively by Houston Industries of the United States.

But Mario Hurtado, a spokesman for Houston Industries, later told Reuters that Venezuela's Electricidad de Caracas was an equal partner in the purchase of Empresas de Energia del Pacifico (Epsa), the main power company in southwest Colombia.

"Generally speaking, this involved an equal partnership between subsidiaries of Houston and Electricidad," Hurtado said, adding that the U.S.-Venezuelan consortium and new owner of Epsa had been named EDC Colombian Energy Ventures.

Epsa has an installed capacity of 900 megawatts and generates and distributes electricity throughout Valle de Cauca province, one of Colombia's leading industrial hubs and an area seen as having enormous growth potential.
The company reported $200 million in energy sales last year and a net profit of more than $100 million.
